newsitem.title: QATAR: Qatar shares clock up solid gains in the week.
newsitem.headline: Qatar shares clock up solid gains in the week.

text.p: Solid gains by leading shares on Qatar's unofficial stock market propelled the index to an all- time high in the week to Thursday, brokers said.
But the trade remained subdued as investors held back from selling in anticipation of further price rises, they said.
The Commercial Bank of Qatar's 18-share index rose by more than two percent to 127.83 points, its highest level since its launch, from 125.14 the previous week.
Dealers attributed the week's rise mainly to a 25-riyal jump in market leader Qatar National Bank's shares to 660.
QNB accounts for nearly 30 percent of the total market capitalisation of around $1.9 billion.

"The increase in the QNB price was on the back of strong rumours that they (QNB) will be distributing one bonus share for every four shares held, in addition to 25 percent of the capital in cash as dividend," said Mazin al-Shakarchi, assistant general manager of treasury and investments at the CBQ.
QNB's annual general meeting is scheduled for March 24.

During the week, 12 shares rose, five remained steady and one declined. Al Khaleej Insurance lost 75 riyals to 240 after distributing cash dividends equal to 25 percent of capital and one bonus share for each held at the end of 1996.

The gainers included Doha Bank Ltd, which added three riyals 308, and Al Ahli Bank of Qatar which rose five riyals to 250. Qatar Islamic Bank was one riyal up at 132 and Qatar International Islamic Bank gathered half a riyal to 86.

Qatar Insurance and Qatar General Insurance advanced five riyals each to 540 and 625 respectively and Qatar Leisure and Qatar Industrial Manufacturing Co added two riyals each to 44 and 60 respectively.
Qatar Cinema gained three riyals to 193 and Qatar Shipping and Qatar Real Estate inched up half a riyal to 48 and 53.50 respectively.
